content.overview: ICA ss. 1–2 — Preliminary and Interpretation is a Senior Counsel-level treatment of s. 1–2 under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. It connects statutory text, doctrine, authority, proof, procedure and remedies without marks-based formatting.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: This topic covers s. 1–2 under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Read the statutory scheme as a coherent allocation of rights, duties, conditions, defences and consequences.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: s. 1–2 must be broken into definitions, operative words, conditions, exceptions, savings and consequences. Map the agreement and commercial records to each statutory ingredient.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body:
1. Establish the transaction and parties.
2. Identify the statutory trigger in s. 1–2.
3. Prove each constituent fact.
4. Test exceptions and defences.
5. Identify the precise legal consequence.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The asserting party ordinarily bears the initial burden on essential facts, subject to admissions and statutory presumptions. Electronic records should be authenticated and presented under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Check jurisdiction, limitation, arbitration or jurisdiction clauses, court fees and the exact relief. Verify the applicable Limitation Act Article and accrual date.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule for sections 1–2: Section 1 states the Act’s short title, extent, commencement and saving; section 2 supplies the interpretation rules used throughout the Act, including proposal, promise, consideration, agreement, contract, void agreement and reciprocal promises.

Definition: Sections 1–2 establish the Act’s identity and the core defined terms that control the later provisions.

Ingredients / conditions:
1. Identify the Act and its temporal and territorial operation.
2. Apply the statutory meanings in section 2 before interpreting later provisions.
3. Distinguish proposal, acceptance, promise, consideration, agreement and contract.
4. Use the defined terms consistently with the statutory context.
